subject.title: Published versions are reserved but unavailable for inspection or discovery

question: Should registry operators treat these publish IDs as an active production consistency incident and reconcile the existing records without deleting or renumbering them?
rationale: Resolving the records requires production data and logs unavailable in the repository review, and choosing a repair action without verifying storage, moderation, and release-row state could destroy evidence or create conflicting releases.

options.title: Inspect and reconcile records
options.body: Audit the supplied publish IDs and restore the existing version records through an idempotent registry repair path before addressing the underlying code or deployment failure.

options.title: Confirm an intentional hold
options.body: If the versions are intentionally hidden by moderation or policy, expose that state to their publishers and document the supported recovery path instead of returning publish success.

options.title: Declare versions unrecoverable
options.body: Only after proving the accepted artifacts cannot be restored, provide an administrator-controlled tombstone or version-release procedure that preserves audit history.

recommendation.title: Inspect and reconcile records
recommendation.body: Audit the supplied publish IDs and restore the existing version records through an idempotent registry repair path before addressing the underlying code or deployment failure.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available ownership signal is recent work on discovery and latest-version summary behavior adjacent to the reported failure.
